title: A mercy so vast it reaches even those who reject Him
subtitle: The name of overflowing mercy that holds every living thing
intro: Ar-Rahman (الرَّحْمَنُ) means the Most Merciful, the One whose mercy is so vast and intense that it reaches every creature: believer and denier, human, animal and plant. Knowing Him by this name changes how you read your own life, including its hardest chapters.

root.sense: Rahma comes from the same root as rahim, the womb. The womb is the first home: a safe place where every need arrives before the child can ask, where it gives nothing back and is still surrounded by care. The form Rahman signals mercy at its most intense and overflowing.

row.title: Hardship means He has left me
Even the wall hides a treasure
sub: His mercy works inside the test

knowing: Ar-Rahman is the name of mercy at full flood. The Arabic form describes something intense and overflowing, mercy so great that the mind cannot measure how much of it you have already received. {idea}It is mercy that does not wait to be earned.{/idea} The one who denies Him still breathes His air, eats His food and sleeps under His roof, all while turning away.

The root takes you back to the womb. There a child is fed without chewing, protected without fighting, and loved without giving anything in return. The mother carries the weight and the child simply receives. That is the picture of rahma: care that gives and expects nothing back. But the womb is only a small trace. The Prophet ﷺ taught that Allah made mercy in a hundred parts and sent down only one, from which every mother, every animal and every creature shows tenderness, keeping ninety-nine for the Day of Judgement (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

Ar-Rahman is usually paired with Ar-Raheem. Many scholars explain that Ar-Rahman is His mercy that covers all of creation, while Ar-Raheem is His constant, special mercy for the believers. {idea}The first is the ocean that surrounds everyone; the second is the river that flows into the hearts of those who turn to Him.{/idea} The name Ar-Rahman belongs to Allah alone; no one else may be called by it.
seeing: When the early Quran was revealed in Makkah, the Arabs did not recognise this name. When told to bow to Ar-Rahman, they asked who Ar-Rahman was (25:60). So the Makkan surahs keep returning to it, as if teaching a new word again and again until it settles in the heart. Even the birds held up in the sky are held, in one verse, by Ar-Rahman (67:19).

A whole surah carries this name, and it is a tour of creation: the sun and moon, the sea and its pearls, the ships, the gift of speech. After each wonder comes the same question, which of your Lord's favours will you deny (55:13). {idea}Day and night, the mother who loves her child after the pain of birth, a hundred flavours where one would do{/idea}: all of it could have been otherwise, and none of it was owed.

The prophets saw His mercy inside their trials. Ayyub, after years of illness, did not say You struck me; he said harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful (21:83). The two orphans in the story of Musa and Al-Khidr lost their father and lived poor, yet a treasure lay under the wall all along, and the Quran calls the whole arrangement a mercy from your Lord (18:82).
trusting: If Ar-Rahman is behind your life, then pain is not a sign that He has forgotten you. {trap}The mind that sees only loss turns bitter and passes its hurt on to others.{/trap} The heart that knows Ar-Rahman looks for the treasure under the wall. Sometimes the mercy is in the healing, and sometimes it is in the illness that taught you what health was worth.

When something is taken, count what was left. A great scholar of the early generations once lost a leg and a son on the same journey and said that Allah had given him four limbs and taken one, seven sons and taken one. That is the glass seen as half full, not by forcing a smile, but by remembering that you started at zero and every good thing since has been a gift. {reward}You stop living as an overthinker and start living as someone who has already been given much.{/reward}
loving: We love those who were good to us before we could ask. That is exactly what He did: He shaped you in the darkness of the womb, fed you there, and brought you out to a world already prepared with air, water, colour and people to love. {reward}When you see that every kindness you have ever received is a drop from His one part of mercy, your heart starts to long for the ninety-nine.{/reward}
now: You are scrolling at 2am, comparing your life with everyone else's highlights and feeling left behind. {idea}Ar-Rahman asks you to put the phone down and count from zero instead{/idea}: the breath you did not earn, the bed under you, the people who would answer if you called. You are not behind. You are held.
old: When life hurts, I feel like I have been forgotten and that mercy is for other people.
new: Ar-Rahman surrounds me even in this; the hardship itself sits inside His mercy, and a treasure may lie under the wall.
try: Write down five things you have today that you did nothing to earn, and say alhamdulillah for each one slowly.

dua.text: Ya Rahman, Your mercy has covered me since the womb. Let me see it in what I have and in what I have lost, and make me merciful to others so that I may be shown mercy.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when you feel overlooked or bitter; it reminds the heart that it has never once lived outside His mercy.

pairs.why: Ar-Rahman is mercy that covers all creation; Ar-Raheem is the constant mercy He brings especially to the believers.
Provision for every creature, including those who deny Him, is one of the clearest signs of His mercy as Ar-Rahman.

faq.a: Ar-Rahman means the Most Merciful, the One whose mercy is vast and intense and reaches every creature in this world, believer and disbeliever, human and animal. It comes from the root r-h-m, which also gives the Arabic word for the womb, a picture of selfless care.

Yes. Scholars agree that the name Ar-Rahman belongs to Allah alone and no created being may be called by it. A person can be described as rahim, merciful, but not as Ar-Rahman. That is why people are named Abdur-Rahman, servant of the Most Merciful.

faq.q: What is the difference between Ar-Rahman and Ar-Raheem?
faq.a: Both come from rahma, mercy. Many scholars explain that Ar-Rahman describes His vast mercy that embraces all of creation, while Ar-Raheem describes His continuous mercy that reaches the believers in particular, through guidance in this life and Paradise in the next.

faq.q: Why is Ar-Rahman repeated so often in the Makkan surahs?
faq.a: The Arabs of Makkah did not know Allah by this name and even asked who Ar-Rahman was when told to bow to Him (25:60). The early surahs, especially Surah Maryam and Surah Ar-Rahman, return to it often, teaching people first and foremost that their Lord is vast in mercy.
